chunks: Al-Naḍr narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
A woman is entitled to a share of the blood money of her husband, and a man is entitled to a share of the blood money of his wife, so long as neither of them has killed the other.

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the husband/man as a legal inheritor in this ruling
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the wife/woman as a legal inheritor in this ruling
key_terms.دِيَةِ امْرَأَتِهِ: the blood money payable for the man's wife
key_terms.دِيَةِ زَوْجِهَا: the blood money payable for the woman's husband
key_terms.صَاحِبَهُ: the other spouse, meaning one's marital partner in this context

ai.seo_question: Can a husband or wife inherit from the blood money of their spouse in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning inheritance from blood money (diyah) between spouses. Each spouse may inherit from the other's diyah, provided that one did not kill the other, which bars such entitlement.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5685 - Al-Nadr narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said: "
A woman is entitled to a share of the blood money (diyyah) of her husband, and a man is entitled to a share of the blood money of his wife, as long as neither of them has killed the other."
